'''Alan Douglas Martin''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 4 December 1937) is a British [[physicist]], currently Emeritus Professor of Physics at the [[University of Durham]].<ref name="staffpage">[https://www.dur.ac.uk/physics/staff/profiles/?id=1816 Staff profile], Durham University, retrieved 2016-02-28</ref>

==Education==
Martin was educated at the [[Eltham College]]. He received his BSc (1958) and PhD (1962) degrees from the [[University College London]].<ref name="whoswho" />

==Work==
Martin is known for his research in the theory of [[elementary particle]]s, which includes studies of [[mesic atom]]s, [[kaon]] physics, [[pi–pi scattering]], [[hadron spectroscopy]] and the anomalous magnetic moment of the [[muon]]. His work on the [[W boson]] and [[top quark]] was used in early [[collider]] experiments.

His ongoing projects include the determination of the [[Parton (particle physics)|parton]] distributions of the proton and studies in [[small x physics|small x]] and [[diffractive physics]], which are relevant to the experiments at the [[Large Hadron Collider]].

He is an author of well-known textbooks on [[particle physics]]. ''Quarks and Leptons'', co-authored with [[Francis Halzen]] in 1984, is a standard text around the world.<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/alan-martin-11891/ |title=Alan Martin |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |location=London }} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where: "All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]."{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160220093712/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=2016-02-20 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Halzen |first=Francis |url=https://www.google.co.cr/books/edition/Quarks_and_Leptons/G7RvQgAACAAJ?hl=en |title=Quarks and Leptons: An Introductory Course in Modern Particle Physics |last2=Martin |first2=Alan Douglas |date=1984 |publisher=Wiley |isbn=978-0-471-81187-9 |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Martin was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2004|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2004]].<ref name="FRS"/> He was awarded the 2007 [[Max Born Prize|Max Born Medal and Prize]] ''for his pioneering research in the understanding of the strong interaction, in particular his theoretical work on the internal structure of the proton.''<ref>[https://www.dur.ac.uk/news/newsitem/?itemno=4905 Leading Durham physicist wins prestigious international award], Durham University</ref>
